_about: Colour and detail rules for the LAC's 3D model. Edit here, then run: python tools/build_model.py "LAC Build Instructions". Rules are tried top to bottom against each CAD mesh name; the first match wins. A mesh whose rule names no colour takes its colours from the "atlas" file (colour-atlas-lac.json): the MRA's atlas for the Nano Board the two kits share, and TechBox's own LAC Cadasio project for the rest. A rule that does name a colour is a TechBox decision or a house-library colour that overrides it (see _notes). First draft, 19 Oct 2026.

rules.match: ^(Part\d+\^(LAC Full Build|LAC Wire Cables)|Copy of Part\d+\^LAC Full Build)$
rules._about: the CAD's own wire bodies (the jumpers, the switch's, potentiometer's and buzzer's leads, the LCD's wires and the USB cable, in every pose the CAD has them): the player draws every wire itself, along the centre lines in wire-paths.json, so that it can move. Not the Dupont caps on their ends (Wire Cap / Wire Cap V2), which are parts.

each resistor's legs, straight (as bought) and bent (Resistor stem 3, as they go into the breadboard): the CAD carries both, one over the other. guide.py draws the legs as wires instead, straight and then bent in Step 4, as the LSM's (Lee, 20 Oct 2026)
the Nano Board: the MRA's export of the same Nano model (nano-mra.glb, extra part NANO), with the MRA's rule and atlas entry
the USB cable's A end (extra part USB_A, the MRA's usb-a-end.glb, the same model as the LAC CAD's own A end NAUO121): overmould black, shell and contacts silver, tongue white. The MRA's rule.
the USB cable's right-angle Mini-B end (NAUO122): the LAC's own (the MRA's and RCC's Mini-B is straight); colours from the LAC atlas: shell silver, overmould black

the half breadboard: body white, legends black, the (+) rail stripes red and the (-) blue, from the LAC atlas. The mesh is the LSM's (extra part NAUO1, breadboard-lsm.glb), its joining tabs on the a side and the column 30 end as the real board has them (Lee, 21 Oct 2026), which changes the mesh's box: atlas_frame lines it up with the atlas by the CAD mesh's own box
the breadboard's joining tabs, two on the a side (the front, +X) and three on the column 30 end (-Z), as on the LSM's breadboard (Lee, 21 Oct 2026): the body's white
the breadboard's protective backing, peeled off in Step 1
the real-time clock module (DS3231, HW-84): colours from the LAC atlas
the 2 resistors: body and colour bands from the LAC atlas (the bands marked skin there); the legs are wires, drawn by guide.py
the potentiometer, its knob, nut and washer: colours from the LAC atlas
the rocker switch: black with white marks, from the LAC atlas
the buzzer: black, with its red and black lead stubs, from the LAC atlas
the LCD's screen (glass), as the house colour library has it

the 20x4 LCD and its I2C backpack: colours from the LAC atlas (board green, bezel black, header pins silver) (the atlas matches the board, bezel and backpack solids exactly but only half of the small solids within 0.6 mm, the CAD and Cadasio boxes differing slightly: atlas_min_match 0.4 takes the nearest solid's colour for each)
the Dupont caps on the ends of the wires: male (Wire Cap V2: housing black, pin silver) and female (Wire Cap, the MRA's part: black), from the LAC atlas

adjusted: NAUO82, NAUO84 (the LCD's GND and VCC wires' male caps): moved 10.16 and 15.23 mm along the (-) blue and (+) red rails, to k = +2 and +4 (z 1290.00, 1295.08), from where the CAD has them (k = -2, z 1279.84), under the legs of the black and green jumpers: neither wire could go in there without passing through them (Lee, 21 Oct 2026, Steps 36 - 37; guide.py LCD_RAIL_SHIFT moves its copy of the caps the same; docs/research/lac/round2/wire_clipping.md).
unconfirmed: Every colour is TechBox's own LAC Cadasio project's, except the Nano Board's (the MRA's, which Lee approved there) and the USB A end's (the MRA's). The female caps are black #1e1616 as in the LAC project; the MRA's same part is dark grey #404040.
decided: 2026-10-13 (Lee, MRA): outline edges use Cadasio's crease angle of 40 degrees on every part.
2026-10-13 (Lee, MRA): colours follow TechBox's own Cadasio project (the atlas file) unless a rule here says otherwise.
2026-10-16 (Lee): the wood plates are roughened ("roughen_mm": 0.1 on the wood rule), as on the MRA and RCC.
_notes.reused: Lee, 19 Oct 2026: the parts the LAC shares with the MRA or RCC use the version made for them. The Nano Board is the MRA's export of the same Nano model (nano-mra.glb, cut by tools/cut_part.py and placed exactly where the LAC CAD's NAUO124 sits: the LAC's own export has 387,505 triangles and the same sliver triangles the RCC's had); the USB cable's A end is the MRA's usb-a-end.glb (the same STEP model as the LAC's NAUO121, fitted to it to 1e-11 mm). The female Dupont cap (Wire Cap) is the MRA's part already. The LAC's right-angle Mini-B plug has no counterpart (the MRA's and RCC's are straight) and stays the LAC's own.
_notes.f4: The CAD has the top panel F4 only once, lying flat beside the base (NAUO50). Seated, it is that same panel moved +117.68 x, -17.26 y, +0.06 z: the rocker switch's two poses (NAUO51 in the flat F4, NAUO46 seated) differ by exactly that move. The guide uses extra part F4 (NAUO50 cut out by tools/cut_part.py into f4.glb, posed by that move).
_notes.missing: Until 19 Oct 2026 the CAD had no F2, F5 or F6; Lee sent each as a STEP of its own (F2.STEP, F5.STEP, F6.STEP: extra parts F2, F5, F6, placed as TechBox's Cadasio project has them).

NAUO1._about: the breadboard, in place of the CAD's NAUO1: the LSM's breadboard as revised (Lee, 20 - 21 Oct 2026: the two joining tabs on the a side and the three on the column 30 end, where the real board has them; the CAD has them on the j side and the column 1 end). The same CAD part, vertex for vertex; cut from lsm.glb by tools/cut_part.py where NAUO1 sits: python tools/cut_part.py "LSM Build Instructions/lsm.glb" BREADBOARD "LAC Build Instructions/breadboard-lsm.glb" --like "LAC Build Instructions/lac-guide.glb" NAUO1. Holes unchanged (wire-paths.json; docs/research/lac/round2/breadboard_tabs.md).

NANO._about: the Nano Board, in place of the CAD's NAUO124: the MRA's export of the same model (mra.glb NAUO126), cut out by tools/cut_part.py where NAUO124 sits: python tools/cut_part.py "MRA Build Instructions Prototype/mra.glb" NAUO126 "LAC Build Instructions/nano-mra.glb" --like "LAC Build Instructions/lac.glb" NAUO124

USB_A._about: the USB cable's A end (the MRA's usb-a-end.glb), where the CAD has its own A end (NAUO121, the same model): fitted to it vertex for vertex. The guide lays it on the table (rest_at).

F4._about: the top panel seated: the CAD's only F4 (NAUO50, lying flat beside the base) cut out by tools/cut_part.py in assembly space (python tools/cut_part.py "LAC Build Instructions/lac.glb" NAUO50 "LAC Build Instructions/f4.glb"), moved onto the frame by the move between the rocker switch's two poses (see _notes.f4)

F5._about: the end panel at the breadboard's end (+z): Lee's F5.STEP (19 Oct 2026; the assembly export had no F5), converted by tools/step_to_glb.py into f5.glb in its own part frame, placed where TechBox's published Cadasio project has F5-1 (its scene is this assembly's frame scaled by 0.6055: fitted on F1, F3, F7 x2, F8 and F9 to 0.0006 mm, and its F4-1 is the seated F4 above to 0.004 mm)

F2._about: the back panel (-x), with the slit the USB cable leaves by: Lee's F2.STEP (19 Oct 2026; the assembly export had no F2), converted by tools/step_to_glb.py into f2.glb in its own part frame, placed where TechBox's published Cadasio project has F2-1 (its scene is this assembly's frame scaled by 0.6055: fitted on F1, F3, F7 x2, F8 and F9 to 0.0006 mm, and its F4-1 is the seated F4 above to 0.004 mm)

F6._about: the end panel at the buzzer's end (-z), with the speaker slots: Lee's F6.STEP (19 Oct 2026; the assembly export had no F6), converted by tools/step_to_glb.py into f6.glb in its own part frame, placed where TechBox's published Cadasio project has F6-1 (its scene is this assembly's frame scaled by 0.6055: fitted on F1, F3, F7 x2, F8 and F9 to 0.0006 mm, and its F4-1 is the seated F4 above to 0.004 mm)
